sentences: In 2010, Country A spent 20% of its budget on schools.
Country B spent only 8%.
drills.hint: Use "while" after a comma to contrast two figures from the same year.

sentences: Football was the top sport among boys.
Most girls preferred swimming.
drills.hint: Give the first fact, add a comma, then "while" and the contrasting fact.

sentences: The forest in the north was cleared for housing.
The lake in the south remained unchanged.
drills.hint: "While" can join two changes on a map that happened in different ways.

sentences: Online sales rose by 15% between 2015 and 2020.
High street sales fell by 5%.
drills.hint: Keep the time phrase in the first clause, then use "while" for the opposite trend.

sentences: Car use in Town C is expected to fall by 2040.
Rail travel there is projected to grow.
answer: Car use in Town C is expected
drills.hint: Keep the future forms in both clauses and join them with "while".

sentences: Rent made up 35% of student spending.
Books made up just 5%.
drills.hint: Use "while" to set a large share against a small one.

sentences: The number of male nurses doubled over the period.
The number of female nurses stayed at about 2,000.
drills.hint: After "while", "the figure" avoids repeating "the number of".

sentences: In 1990, 60% of households owned a car.
Only 10% owned a computer.
drills.hint: Put a comma before "whereas" to contrast two percentages.

sentences: Product X sold 500 units in January.
Product Y sold just 120 units.
drills.hint: "Whereas" links two facts that differ; keep the comma before it.

sentences: The 18-24 age group used social media daily.
Most people over 65 rarely used it.
drills.hint: Contrast the two age groups with "whereas"; "it" refers to social media.

sentences: Coal produced most electricity in 2000.
Wind power produced very little.
drills.hint: Use "whereas" after a comma when the second fact is the opposite of the first.

sentences: Rural areas saw a sharp fall in population.
Urban areas grew steadily.
drills.hint: One clause uses adjective + noun ("a sharp fall"), the other verb + adverb.

sentences: Spending on gas is projected to rise to £800.
Spending on oil is expected to remain stable.
drills.hint: Keep both future forms and put the comma before "whereas".

sentences: Teenagers in Group A read for two hours a week.
Those in Group B read for six hours.
drills.hint: "Those" replaces "teenagers" in the clause after "whereas".

sentences: The price of petrol rose sharply in 2008.
The price of diesel fell slightly.
drills.hint: Use a semicolon before "in contrast," to join two opposite trends.

sentences: Cinema visits declined over the decade.
Streaming subscriptions tripled in the same period.
drills.hint: After the semicolon, "in contrast," introduces the opposite trend.

sentences: In Town C, most people commuted by car.
In Town D, most people cycled.
drills.hint: Use a semicolon, then "in contrast," and the habit in the second town.

sentences: Exports of Product X grew steadily after 2012.
Imports of the product fell to 2,000 tonnes.
drills.hint: Two opposite trends: a semicolon, then "in contrast" with a comma.

sentences: Group A spent most of its income on housing.
Group B spent most of its income on food.
drills.hint: "In contrast to" is followed by a noun; the main clause comes after the comma.

sentences: The share of adults who smoked halved by 2015.
The share who vaped rose to 12%.
answer: The share of adults who smoked
drills.hint: Use "the share/proportion" for percentages and a semicolon before "in contrast,".

sentences: In 2020, 45% of workers worked from home.
In 2010, the figure was only 10%.
drills.hint: "Compared with" adds the earlier figure after a comma, with no new verb.

sentences: Product X sold 3,000 units in May.
Product Y sold 1,200 units in May.
drills.hint: Put the larger figure first, then "compared with" and the smaller one.

sentences: Women made up 60% of university graduates.
Men made up 40%.
drills.hint: Use "compared with" plus a figure, then "for" to name the second group.

sentences: Water use in Town C was 150 litres per person.
Water use in Town D was only 90 litres.
answer: the 90 litres used in Town D,
drills.hint: A fronted "compared with" phrase needs a comma before the main clause.

sentences: Rail fares rose by 30% over the decade.
Bus fares rose by only 12%.
drills.hint: "Compared with" lets you add a second percentage without a new verb.

sentences: Ten thousand tourists visited the museum in 2019.
Only 4,000 visited in 2021.
drills.hint: Use "compared with" to add the later figure to the same sentence.

sentences: In Country A, 70% of energy came from coal.
In Country B, coal supplied just 20%.
drills.hint: Make "coal" the subject so that one verb covers both countries.

sentences: Coal was the main source of electricity, at 40%.
Gas was second, at 25%.
drills.hint: "Followed by" introduces the next item in a ranking.

sentences: First, the leaves are picked by hand.
Then they are dried in the sun.
drills.hint: After "followed by", use an -ing form or a noun for the next stage.

sentences: Sales peaked in December.
There was a sharp fall in January.
drills.hint: Use "followed by" plus a noun phrase for the next change.

sentences: Housing made up the largest share of costs.
Transport made up the second largest share.
drills.hint: Rank the categories: the biggest first, then "followed by" the next.

sentences: Unemployment rose sharply in 2009.
A slow recovery followed over the next five years.
drills.hint: "Followed by" adds what happened next without a new verb.

sentences: The old factory was demolished.
A shopping centre was then built on the site.
answer: a shopping centre on the site.
drills.hint: After "followed by", turn the second action into a noun phrase.

sentences: Product X had the most complaints, at 320.
Product Y had 210 complaints.
drills.hint: Use "followed by" for second place and "with" for its figure.

sentences: Sales rose to a peak of 800 units in 2015.
They then fell to 500 units in 2020.
drills.hint: After "before", use an -ing form, not a past tense verb.

sentences: The population of Town C grew steadily until 1990.
It then levelled off at 50,000.
drills.hint: "Before" + -ing shows the next stage of the trend.

sentences: The glass is cleaned.
Then it is crushed into small pieces.
drills.hint: In a process, use "before being" + past participle for a passive next step.

sentences: Coal use fell gradually until 2010.
It then dropped sharply to 15%.
drills.hint: Use "before" + -ing to describe what the line did next.

sentences: Rents in Town C are expected to rise until 2030.
They are then projected to stabilise.
answer: Rents in Town C are expected
drills.hint: Use "before" + -ing after a future form to show the next change.

sentences: The number of visitors climbed to 2 million in 2018.
It then fell back to 1.5 million.
drills.hint: Join two stages of a trend with "before" and an -ing verb.

sentences: The milk is heated to 72°C.
Then it is cooled and bottled.
drills.hint: The passive -ing form "being" + past participle follows "before".

sentences: Profits fell to £2 million in 2009.
They then recovered to £5 million by 2012.
drills.hint: A fronted "after" + -ing phrase needs a comma and the same subject as the main clause.

sentences: The bricks are shaped in moulds.
Then they are dried for 48 hours.
drills.hint: Use "after being" + past participle to start with the earlier stage.

sentences: Car sales dipped in 2020.
They rose sharply in 2021.
drills.hint: "After" + -ing puts the earlier event at the end of the sentence.

sentences: The water is filtered through sand.
It is then stored in large tanks.
drills.hint: Put the later stage first, then "after being" + past participle for the earlier one.

sentences: Membership peaked at 900 in 2016.
It then declined steadily to 400.
drills.hint: The subject after the comma must be the thing that peaked.

sentences: Solar power is expected to overtake gas by 2030.
It is then projected to reach 40% by 2040.
drills.hint: "After" + -ing works for projections too; keep "is projected to" in the main clause.

sentences: In 2015, 55% of students passed the exam.
This was the highest figure in the period.
drills.hint: Use ", which" to comment on the whole figure just given.

sentences: Tourist numbers fell by half in 2020.
This was the sharpest drop on the graph.
drills.hint: "Which" after a comma refers back to the whole change.

sentences: A new road was built through the village.
This divided the farmland into two parts.
drills.hint: Use "which" for a thing or an event; never use "who" for it.

sentences: Country A recycled 62% of its waste.
This was twice the rate of Country B.
drills.hint: Non-defining clauses take a comma and "which", not "that".

sentences: Online sales are expected to reach 50% by 2030.
This would be double the 2020 figure.
drills.hint: "Which" can comment on a projection; keep "would" in the relative clause.

sentences: Some households had no internet access.
They made up 12% of the total.
drills.hint: A defining clause takes no commas: it tells us which households.

sentences: The 25-34 age group spent £120 a month online.
This was more than any other group.
drills.hint: Point back to the whole figure with ", which", not to the people.

sentences: Water consumption rose to 300 litres per day.
This marked the peak for the whole period.
drills.hint: After the comma, "which" + verb adds a comment on the figure.

sentences: The total energy output was 500 units.
Coal accounted for 40% of this.
drills.hint: "With" + noun + -ing adds a detail about the total.

sentences: Most visitors came from Europe.
Asia provided 25% of the total.
drills.hint: After "with", use a noun and an -ing verb, not a past tense.

sentences: Sales rose in all five regions.
The North recorded the largest increase.
drills.hint: Use "with" to highlight one detail of the general trend.

sentences: Car ownership increased steadily over the decade.
The figure reached 1.2 million by 2020.
drills.hint: "With the figure" + -ing adds the final number to a trend.

sentences: Household waste was made up of five types.
Food waste was the largest, at 35%.
drills.hint: "With" + noun + "being" adds a detail about one category.

sentences: Spending on leisure doubled between 2000 and 2020.
Travel made up most of the increase.
drills.hint: Use "with" + noun + -ing to explain which part caused most of the change.

sentences: Three new schools opened in the town.
Two of them were built in the east.
drills.hint: "With" can be followed by a noun and a past participle for a passive detail.

sentences: Online sales grew steadily from 2015.
They reached £40 million in 2022.
drills.hint: After a comma, use the -ing form to add the end point of the trend.

sentences: The temperature rose throughout the morning.
It peaked at 31°C at 2 pm.
drills.hint: Use "peaking at" after a comma rather than a second past tense verb.

sentences: Unemployment declined sharply after 2012.
It fell to 4% in 2018.
drills.hint: "Falling to" adds the lowest point without starting a new clause.

sentences: Visitor numbers climbed rapidly in the summer.
They peaked at 12,000 in August.
drills.hint: The -ing clause "peaking at" gives the highest point of the rise.

sentences: The number of electric cars is expected to rise.
It is projected to reach 5 million by 2035.
drills.hint: A participle clause works with projections too: add "reaching" + the figure.

sentences: The proportion of smokers dropped steadily.
It fell to 14% by 2020.
drills.hint: Use "the proportion of" for percentages, then "falling to" for the final level.

sentences: Rice exports increased sharply in 2010.
They reached a peak of 9,000 tonnes.
drills.hint: Use "reaching a peak of" after a comma to add the highest figure.

sentences: Gas prices dropped gradually throughout the year.
They fell to a low of £60 in December.
drills.hint: After a comma, "falling to" adds the final low point of the decline.

sentences: The share of renewable energy rose sharply.
It reached a record 30% in 2020.
drills.hint: The -ing clause shares the subject of the main clause, so no new subject is needed.

sentences: The raw cotton is cleaned.
Then it is spun into thread.
drills.hint: "And then" links two stages; the second "is" can be left out.

sentences: Bus use fell slightly in 2015.
Then it recovered to its earlier level.
drills.hint: Use "and then" to show the next movement of the same line.

sentences: Prices remained stable for three years.
Then they rose by 20% in 2019.
drills.hint: "And then" joins two verbs with the same subject; no comma is needed.

sentences: The sugar cane is harvested by machine.
Next, it is transported to the mill.
drills.hint: With "and then" in a passive process, "is" is not repeated.

sentences: The car park was extended in 2005.
It was then turned into a garden in 2015.
drills.hint: Describe two changes to one place in time order with "and then".

sentences: Membership doubled between 2000 and 2005.
It then levelled off at around 600.
drills.hint: "And then" keeps the same subject for both stages of the trend.

sentences: Spending on books fell by 30%.
Spending on e-books rose by 50%.
drills.hint: Use a semicolon, then "by contrast," before the opposite trend.

sentences: Men worked an average of 42 hours a week.
Women worked 34 hours on average.
drills.hint: "By contrast," after a semicolon sets one group against another.

sentences: The west of the island was heavily developed.
The east remained largely untouched.
drills.hint: On a map, "by contrast" sets one area against another.

sentences: Group A's scores improved steadily.
Group B's scores fluctuated throughout.
drills.hint: "Those of" avoids repeating "scores" after "by contrast,".

sentences: Exports from Port X rose by 20%.
Exports from Port Y fell by 8%.
drills.hint: "By contrast" can sit after the subject of the second clause, between commas.

sentences: Demand for oil is projected to decline.
Demand for hydrogen is expected to soar.
drills.hint: Keep the future forms and put "by contrast," after the semicolon.

sentences: Coal use fell over the period.
Renewable energy use rose over the period.
drills.hint: Start a summary with "Overall," and give the main trends, not figures.

sentences: The number of cars in Town C increased.
The number of bicycles decreased.
drills.hint: "Overall," is one word followed by a comma; never say "in overall".

sentences: Product X was the best seller in every month.
Sales of all products rose over the year.
drills.hint: An overview gives the general trend and the main feature, without exact figures.

sentences: Most age groups watched less television.
Only the over-65s watched more.
drills.hint: Begin with "Overall," then contrast the main pattern with the exception.

sentences: Urban populations are expected to grow.
Rural populations are projected to shrink.
drills.hint: An overview of projections keeps future forms such as "are expected to".

sentences: Spending on all services increased.
Health spending stayed the highest throughout.
drills.hint: A good overview gives the general trend plus the biggest category.

sentences: The process has six stages.
It begins with harvesting and ends with packaging.
drills.hint: For a process overview, give the number of stages and the first and last ones.

sentences: The chart shows sales of three products.
Product X sold the most.
drills.hint: "As can be seen" + where to look, then a comma and the main point.

sentences: The graph shows rail passenger numbers.
Numbers rose sharply after 2015.
drills.hint: Use "from the graph" or "in the chart" after "as can be seen".

sentences: The table gives figures for five cities.
City E had the lowest crime rate.
drills.hint: The phrase "as can be seen" points the reader to the data before the main fact.

sentences: The pie charts compare energy use in 2000 and 2020.
The share of solar power grew significantly.
drills.hint: Name the visual after "as can be seen", add a comma, then give the key change.

sentences: The table shows rail fares from 2010 to 2020.
Fares rose every year.
drills.hint: "As can be seen" can sit between the subject and the verb, with commas around it.

sentences: The maps show the town centre in 1990 and today.
Most of the shops have been replaced by cafés.
drills.hint: Use "on the map" for maps and the present perfect for changes up to now.

sentences: Sales of Product X doubled in 2019.
Sales of Product Y rose by 90%.
drills.hint: "Similarly," after a semicolon links two trends that move the same way.

sentences: Car use in Town C fell by 10%.
Car use in Town D also fell, by 12%.
drills.hint: After "similarly," you can change the structure, e.g. "saw a fall".

sentences: Adults in Group A slept seven hours a night.
Adults in Group B slept about the same amount.
drills.hint: Use "similarly," when the second group shows the same pattern.

sentences: The price of bread rose steadily.
The price of milk climbed gradually.
drills.hint: Two rising prices: join them with a semicolon and "similarly,".

sentences: The school in the north was enlarged.
The hospital was also extended.
drills.hint: On a map, "similarly," links two buildings that changed in the same way.

sentences: The 25-34 group preferred online shopping.
The 18-24 group preferred it as well.
drills.hint: "Similarly" can go before the main verb of the second clause, with no commas.

sentences: Factory jobs fell between 1990 and 2010.
Service jobs doubled in the same period.
drills.hint: "At the same time," shows two changes happening in the same period.

sentences: Petrol prices rose sharply in 2022.
Sales of electric cars rose in the same year.
drills.hint: Use a semicolon before "at the same time," to link two changes in one year.

sentences: The town's population grew by 20%.
The number of schools stayed the same.
drills.hint: "At the same time," can link a change with something that did not change.

sentences: Group A's income rose by 5%.
Its spending rose by 9% over the same period.
drills.hint: Use "at the same time," to compare two figures for one group.

sentences: The number of older people is set to rise.
The working population is expected to shrink.
drills.hint: Keep both future forms and link them with "at the same time,".

sentences: Online banking grew rapidly.
Many bank branches closed.
drills.hint: "At the same time as" is followed by a full clause, then a comma and the main clause.

sentences: Men spent 3 hours a day online.
Women spent 4 hours a day online.
drills.hint: "Respectively" goes at the end and matches the figures to the groups in order.

sentences: Product X cost £12 in 2010.
Product Y cost £15 in 2010.
drills.hint: Join the two subjects and the two prices, then end with "respectively".

sentences: Group A scored 65% on the test.
Group B scored 72%.
drills.hint: Keep the groups and the scores in the same order, then add "respectively".

sentences: Gas made up 30% of energy use.
Oil made up 25%.
drills.hint: The first figure belongs to the first noun, the second to the second.

sentences: Visits to Museum A rose by 10%.
Visits to Museum B rose by 18%.
answer: Visits to Museums A and B
drills.hint: Make "Museums" plural, give both figures, then end with "respectively".

sentences: Solar power is expected to supply 20% by 2040.
Wind power is expected to supply 25%.
drills.hint: Join the subjects with "and", make the verb plural, and end with "respectively".

sentences: Coal was the largest source of power.
It accounted for 45% of the total.
drills.hint: Use "accounting for" after a comma to add the share, not a past tense verb.

sentences: Online sales grew rapidly.
They accounted for 30% of all sales by 2020.
drills.hint: The -ing form "accounting for" adds the share reached by the end of the period.

sentences: Rice was the main crop in Region C.
It took up 60% of farmland.
drills.hint: "Accounting for" + percentage shows how big the main category was.

sentences: The over-65s were the fastest-growing group.
They made up 22% of the population in 2020.
drills.hint: After the comma, "accounting for" replaces "they made up".

sentences: Food waste was the biggest category.
It made up over a third of all waste.
drills.hint: Use "accounting for" + a fraction or percentage after the comma.

sentences: Electric cars are expected to grow in number.
They will account for half of new sales by 2035.
drills.hint: The -ing form "accounting for" also works in a sentence about the future.

sentences: Tourism earned £40 million in Town C.
This was 35% of the town's income.
drills.hint: Give the amount first, then its share with "accounting for".

sentences: Group A had 400 members.
Group B had 200 members.
drills.hint: Use "as many as" for countable nouns like members; never "than" after it.

sentences: Country A produced 6,000 tonnes of wheat.
Country B produced 3,000 tonnes.
drills.hint: Use "as much as" for uncountable amounts such as wheat.

sentences: In 2000, 800 students took the course.
By 2020, only 400 took it.
drills.hint: Use "half the figure" (no "of") to compare a number with an earlier one.

sentences: Sales of Product X were 2,000 in 2015.
They were 4,000 in 2020.
drills.hint: When a figure goes from 2,000 to 4,000, it has doubled.

sentences: Region A received 900 mm of rain.
Region B received 300 mm.
drills.hint: Use "three times as much as" with an uncountable noun like rain.

sentences: Shop X sold 150 laptops in March.
Shop Y sold 300 laptops.
drills.hint: Laptops are countable, so use "half as many as".

sentences: There were 2 million online learners in 2020.
This number is expected to double by 2030.
drills.hint: The verb is "double"; "twice" and "half" are not verbs.

sentences: Unemployment among the 18-24 age group was 12%.
The overall rate was 6%.
drills.hint: Say "twice the rate" with no "of" after "twice".

sentences: Household A used 200 kWh of electricity.
Household B used 400 kWh.
drills.hint: 200 is 50% of 400, so use "half the amount".
